title: Punish One, Teach a Hundred: The Sobering Effect of Peer Punishment on the Unpunished
authors: Francesco D’Acunto; Michael Weber; Jin Xie
near_miss_reason: Stacked design in every reported column (cohort-specific +/-6-year windows appended; cohort-by-year with cohort-by-prefecture or cohort-by-firm FE; Table 3, Figure 2, Tables 4-9; the article proposes 'a stacked DiD approach'); the coefficient of interest is a triple difference (AfterPeerPunishment x SOE) with AfterPeerPunishment entered as a second staggered treatment regressor; all columns include time-varying firm controls (LnAssets, LongtermDebt, Cash_Assets, TobinQ, ST, SOE indicator). Staggered binary exposure: a listed firm's prefecture experiences its first SOE punishment in cohort years 2001-2017, firms in never-punished prefectures as controls; no unstacked firm-year TWFE is reported. Firm-year raw data are shipped.
eligible_reason: The exposure is staggered and binary (a listed firm's prefecture experiences its first SOE punishment for fraudulent loan guarantees in year minSOEpunishyear, cohorts 2001-2017, with firms in never-punished prefectures as controls), but every reported regression is a stacked DiD (cohort-specific +/-6-year windows appended; FE cohort x year with cohort x prefecture, cohort x firm, or cohort x prefecture x year), the coefficient of interest is a triple difference (AfterPeerPunishment x SOE) with AfterPeerPunishment as a second staggered regressor, and all columns include time-varying firm controls (LnAssets LongtermDebt Cash_Assets TobinQ ST and the SOE indicator). Stacking, DDD with an additional staggered regressor, and controls each exclude the specification; no unstacked TWFE is reported.
design_notes: Single master do-file DoFile_20250622.do (1,516 lines, Stata 14.2). Part 1 builds StackedSample1 from RawData.dta (42,589 firm-years, 3,801 listed firms, 1990-2018, 289 prefectures): for each cohort year i in 2001-2017, treated = firms with minSOEpunishyear==i kept for years i-6..i+6; controls = firms whose prefecture is never punished (minSOEpunishyear==9999) or punished after i+6, same window; cohorts with no treated or no control dropped; eventyr = year - cohortnew; post = year>=cohortnew; treat = firm located in a punished prefecture; AfterPeerPunishment = post*treat; AfterPeerPunishment_SOE = AfterPeerPunishment*SOEdummy; sample excludes punished firms themselves, event year 0, firms listed after the cohort year, and cross-listed (BH) firms. Table 3 (lines 643-659): xi: reghdfe Guarantees_Assets AfterPeerPunishment_SOE AfterPeerPunishment SOEdummy LnAssets LongtermDebt Cash_Assets TobinQ ST, keepsingletons a(cohortnew##i.year cohortnew##city) cluster(city); then a(cohortnew##i.year cohortnew##i.firmid); then a(cohortnew##i.city##i.year cohortnew##i.firmid); repeated for Guarantees_Assets10. Figure 2: pre-trend event study with pre6..post_6 dummies, a(treat##i.eventyr cohortnew##i.city##i.year cohortnew##i.firmid). Table 4 robustness: at least one punishment, excluding Beijing/Shanghai/Shenzhen, fixed initial SOE status. StackedSample2 (Orbis related-party outcomes, Table 9 cols 4-6) and StackedSample3 (Figure A.3) follow the same construction. Outcome Guarantees_Assets = loan guarantees provided to related parties / assets (winsorized); Guarantees_Assets10 = indicator >10%.
estimators_reported: stacked_triple_difference (reghdfe, cohort x year and cohort x firm/prefecture FE, time-varying controls)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Cohorts are first-punishment years 2001-2017 at the prefecture level (up to 17; those without treated or control firms dropped). Firms in never-punished prefectures (minSOEpunishyear==9999) serve as controls.

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked design; triple difference with AfterPeerPunishment as additional staggered regressor; time-varying firm controls
specs.treatment_definition: firm in a prefecture whose first SOE punishment for fraudulent loan guarantees occurred in cohort year, years after that year
specs.fe: cohortnew##i.year with cohortnew##city (cols 1,4), cohortnew##i.firmid (cols 2,5), or cohortnew##i.city##i.year + cohortnew##i.firmid (cols 3,6)
specs.controls: SOEdummy LnAssets LongtermDebt Cash_Assets TobinQ ST
specs.sample_condition: StackedSample1: sample==1 (non-punished, listed before cohort year, non-BH firms, eventyr in [-6,6] excluding 0)
specs.notes: Table 4 Panels A-C and Tables 5-9 reuse the structure with sample restrictions or interactions

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked design; controls; event-time dummies interacted within stacked cohorts
specs.treatment_var: pre6 pre5 pre4 pre3 pre2 zero post_1 ... post_6
specs.controls: SOEdummy LnAssets LongtermDebt Cash_Assets TobinQ ST

data_access: proprietary (CSMAR and Orbis licensed), but the processed firm-year raw files used to build every stacked sample are shipped
replication_feasible: no (no eligible specification; an unstacked firm-year TWFE with a single AfterPeerPunishment regressor could be constructed but is not reported)
screener_notes: Article text not available; table numbers come from the do-file section headers. The paper's object of interest is the differential SOE response (triple difference) and the authors note that information and local shocks are common to peer SOEs and non-SOEs, so the simple peer-punishment DiD is only a nuisance regressor here.
hand_check_nov4: Near-miss (stacked; DDD with a second staggered regressor; controls). Record coded under the earlier rule with near_miss false; every column is a stacked triple difference with controls, so the staggered binary exposure fails only on restrictions. Not controls-only.
